doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: The Three Wishes book, meeting his wife and staying with the Jazztet
summary: He found himself in the Baroness Rothschild's book, met his wife while with the Jazztet, made two records and the Perception date with Art Farmer, and states his rule not to leave a job.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I’m still single at the time, yeah. So then when I got with the Jazztet, that was, as a matter of fact there’s a book out now that was put out by the Baroness Rothschild called © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Musicians’ Three Wishes. And she would go around with a camera and ask the musicians if they had three wishes what would that be. And come to find out I’m in the book. I never had no idea. I don’t even recall her or anybody talking to me. Because see here again, I would go to hear Thelonious Monk I would sit at the table with the band but I was well reserved and I knew how to keep my mouth shut and not speak until I was spoken to. And see even then, the older musicians liked me because I wasn’t one to run my mouth, like I knew, I would listen, and when they spoke to me. So I said, “Are you kidding?” and Michael West said, “Yeah Mabern, you’re in that book.” There’s two beautiful pictures, one with me and Charlie Rouse and one with me and Teddy Wilson, another one of my heroes, you know. Shortly after that we went to the Lionel jazz festival and we left there and probably went to Chicago and that’s where I met my wife, when I was with the Jazztet. And I used to say Benny Golson — then I thought about it and I said, now Benny Golson’s on the spot. He’s responsible for hiring me, but it was Cedar Walton that made it possible for me to sit in. So I said, “Cedar I’ve been with my wife almost fifty years, maybe because of you.” He said, “Brother Mabern, I didn’t know that.” So that’s how, and then I stayed with the band until it disbanded. I was with the band, we did two records together with the band and I did one beautiful quartet date with Art Farmer called “Perception” with Roy McCurdy, Tommy Williams and myself. A beautiful date. And like I always told Sonny [inaudible], he likes it, I said well, on any kind of job don’t leave the job unless the job leaves you. That’s my philosophy. As long as the job is going, don’t leave the job. Why should I go looking for something that already — you know what I mean? So I never quit a job, I stayed until it was over then I moved on to the next gig.
